defects.claim_says: section 2 of EO 10804 'revokes 9721 and 10103 insofar as they affect employees covered by section 6(a) of the International Atomic Energy Agency Participation Act of 1957' ('an express revocation, but only insofar as the orders affect employees covered by section 6(a)'; 'earlier revoked the order only in part')
defects.source_says: EO 10804 section 2 (24 FR 1147) reads 'Executive Order No. 9721 of May 10, 1946; Executive Order No, 10103 of February 1, 1950; and Executive Order No. 10774 of July 25, 1958, insofar as it affects any employee covered by section 6(a) of the International Atomic Energy Agency Participation Act of 1957 ... are revoked except that each shall be considered to remain in effect with respect to any employee ... who does not elect to have coverage ... and for the purposes of any rights and benefits vested'. The singular 'insofar as it affects' qualifier follows the semicolon-separated list and attaches to EO 10774 only. EO 9721 and EO 10103 are revoked generally, subject only to the two saving exceptions; they are not revoked solely as to section 6(a) IAEA employees.

reasoning: The genuine version differs from the planted control only in the end dates, which are now 1986-02-25 throughout. Those dates are correct: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986 lists both 9721 and 10103 and any amendments, has no effective-date wording and no savings clause. Identity (15 FR 597, signed February 1, 1950) and the three-clause inventory (enacting paragraph, amendment 1 adding the leave-of-absence sentence, amendment 2 reviving section 2) are correct. The EO 11138 and EO 11303 later events and dates agree with the held texts, and the cruden search shows no other order acting on 10103. I also agree that 1986 is the defensible end. EO 10804 keeps each order 'in effect' for non-electing employees serving on the enactment date and for vested rights, and the 1964 and 1966 waivers show the amended order still being applied, so EO 10804 is not the first end of every command. The claim nevertheless misstates EO 10804's operative scope. It reads the IAEA section 6(a) qualifier as limiting the revocation of 9721 and 10103, so that 10804 revoked them 'only in part'. The text attaches that qualifier, in the singular, to EO 10774 alone; 9721 and 10103 were revoked generally, subject to the savings. The later event should state a general revocation with saving exceptions. The rationale and judgment_reason must describe the mechanism accurately. The outcome does not change, but a misstated mechanism for a recorded event is a defect under the review standard. Also noted, not as a defect: the strike-and-insert ruling contemplates before-and-after text for amendment events, which the claim does not record.
